hypothesis: session.cold_open_10mib (~25.2s launch_to_ready on the 10MiB fixture, ~90ms first paint) may measure the wrong user path: the synthetic fixture (session_size.py/corpus.py) has NO compaction row, so Prime Agent Rust's windowed-resume open (pa-core/src/session/window.rs WindowedSessionStore::open via pa-daemon SessionFile::open_windowed at worker.rs:2229) never finds a firstKeptEntryId boundary, retains every row, and full-parses the whole file; real sessions that hit a compaction boundary open near-instantly (user report: parse-from-end-to-most-recent-compaction makes session opens fast). Suite may measure the no-compaction worst case, not common large-session resume.
approach: Read-path audit + 3-fixture measurement on ONE VM (same binary, sequential, load-gated, 5 trials each): (a) stock 10MiB fixture (no compaction), (b) new compacted-boundary variant (session-10mib-compacted: same corpus generator/seed + one byte-plausible compaction row whose firstKeptEntryId pins a ~102KiB retained window; bulk pad in the discarded prefix; sentinel rides the retained tail), (c) a REAL session snapshot from the orchestrator box (2.89MiB, 2343 rows, v3 header, chain intact, ZERO compaction entries). Ready contract identical across all three (typed-echo probe after first paint; tail sentinel proof).
parity_notes: No product code changed. Harness additions only: bench/adapters/fixtures/session_size.py gains build_session_compacted + SessionSizeCompactedFixture (generator session-size-compacted/1, own sha256 manifest; stock generator/bytes untouched - stock fixture sha256 re-verified identical after the edit); bench/adapters/benchmarks/session_open_compacted.py adds session.cold_open_10mib_compacted as a SessionColdOpen subclass (same measure(), same driver/ready contract; existing suite semantics unchanged). validity.notes: All four measurements: ONE VM (ei70x1q2q21ing940crob3aw, 16c/32GB), SAME pinned binary 3940a1f2 (sha256 206696db...), sequential, load-gated, 5 trials each (3 for the t400 scaling point), identical ready contract (typed-echo probe after first paint + tail sentinel proof; every trial validated sentinel+echo+erase). Calibration median 1.064s (3x python sum loop). (c) used per-trial copies (fresh inode, original file never modified); (a)/(b) measured through the canonical suites, which append creation-prefix rows to the fixture per trial (+1278B after 5 stock trials) - pre-existing harness behavior; the window sidecar written each trial goes stale on the next append, so every trial re-scans cold (trials homogeneous: stock spread 21293-21839ms, compacted 317-321ms). Harness wart found: SessionSizeFixture.ensure() returns the stale manifest without re-validating the file hash once trials have appended rows, so repeated campaigns on the same bench root resume a mutated fixture under the original sha256 evidence - latent reproducibility wart, negligible numeric impact (~256B/trial). Product-version cosmetic: version_info reports the product.yaml revision pin (7152746b), not the actual binary commit (3940a1f2, binary_sha256 is the true provenance). My committed fixture had a bug on first deploy (ensure() returned the generate() Path instead of the manifest dict) - fixed before commit; VM harness re-synced and both suites re-ran clean after the fix.

decision: VERDICT: hypothesis CONFIRMED with a mechanism twist. (1) The stock session.cold_open_10mib measures the no-compaction path: adding ONE byte-plausible compaction boundary row to the SAME 10MiB corpus drops p50 launch_to_ready 21393.2ms -> 318.2ms (67x). The stock 25.2s campaign baseline (7152746b) and 21.4s here are the no-boundary full-retention resume, not the common post-compaction resume (~0.32s, faster than a fresh-session cold start baseline 341.5ms). (2) TWIST: the dominant 21s is NOT the JSONL parse - a VM-scratch example shows SessionFile::open_windowed on the no-boundary 10MiB fixture costs 96.6ms (full parse 25.6ms, context build 46ms). The 21s lives in the retained-transcript resume pipeline (daemon replay + TUI transcript build/render) whose cost explodes superlinearly with retained message count: 135 msgs -> 0.26s net, 519 -> 0.26s, 1406 -> 0.33s, 7259 -> 21.3s (~n^2.5 between 1.4k and 7.3k). The compaction boundary fixes it by shrinking retained rows 7259 -> 135. (3) Real-device answer: a no-compaction large session is NOT slow at the file-open layer (windowed reverse scan + full-retention parse of 10MiB = ~97ms; real 2.89MiB/1406-msg no-compaction session opens end-to-end in 0.39s). It BECOMES slow only when thousands of messages stay retained (>= ~2-7k), which auto-compaction at the context limit should normally prevent (real sessions on the orchestrator box never exceed ~1.4k retained msgs without compaction). (4) RE-RANK RECOMMENDATION: the session-open optimization lane should be re-ranked/re-scoped - parse-side work buys <=100ms; the common large-session resume is already ~0.32s; the remaining real optimization target is the superlinear retained-transcript replay/render pipeline for the pre-first-compaction / compaction-disabled large session, and any lane optimizing it should be measured against the new compacted suite (common path) AND the stock suite (worst case), never the stock number alone.

correction.note: The ~n^2.5 retained-message-count conclusion and >=2-7k threshold in decision/scaling_net_resume_cost are FALSE causal claims. The 10MiB stock fixture has a single ~4.3MB unbroken text token; its first TUI frame spends ~30s in quadratic markdown wrapping. A real no-compaction 2717-message session renders in 4.7ms; a 50MiB toolResult-heavy fixture renders in 13.7ms because tool cards cap results. Compaction removes the stock monoword; retained count is confounded, not the cause. See superseding record.
